# Tracing quickstart - Docs by LangChain
**URL:** https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-quickstart

---

LangSmith gives you end-to-end visibility into your agent by capturing

[*traces*](/langsmith/observability-concepts#traces); a complete record of every step that ran during a request, from the inputs passed in to the final output returned. In this quickstart, you will add tracing to an AI assistant and view the results in LangSmith. Traces belong to an

[agent and one of its environments](/langsmith/agent-registry)within a workspace. This quickstart creates the agent in LangSmith, then configures your code to send traces to its identifier and environment. Compatibility instructions cover older workspaces and self-hosted LangSmith.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:
- **A LangSmith account**: Sign up or log in at [smith.langchain.com](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-observability-quickstart).
- **A LangSmith API key**: Follow the [Create an API key](/langsmith/create-account-api-key) guide.
- **A model provider API key**: Generate one from the [OpenAI dashboard](https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys), the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys), or [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) for Gemini.

Select your provider in the tabs on each step. The Anthropic and Gemini examples are in Python and TypeScript only, because the LangSmith Java SDK wraps only the OpenAI client.

## 1. Set up your environment

1. 
Create a directory for your agent code, install the dependencies, and configure the required environment variables:
  - OpenAI
  - Anthropic
  - Gemini
2. 
Export your environment variables in your shell:
  - OpenAI
  - Anthropic
  - Gemini

   Before sending traces, create the agent in LangSmith:
  1. 
In an [agent-based workspace](/langsmith/agent-registry), open **+ Agent**, choose **Observability**, and create an agent with an **Agent name** and **Agent ID**. This requires the `projects:create` permission. If the agent already exists, reuse it.
  2. 
Copy the **Agent ID** and choose an environment: `local`, `development`, `staging`, or `production`.
  3. 
Configure [agent addressing](/langsmith/log-traces-to-agent) before running the agent:

   Register the agent once, not for every trace. Remove`LANGSMITH_PROJECT`, `LANGCHAIN_PROJECT`, and `LANGCHAIN_SESSION` from the environment where your code runs. Do not combine legacy destination settings with agent addressing. To create the agent with an SDK call or API request, see [Create an agent programmatically](/langsmith/create-an-agent#create-an-agent-programmatically). Project-based workspaces and self-hosted LangSmith Agent addressing is available in agent-based workspaces on LangSmith Cloud. In a project-based workspace, including self-hosted LangSmith, set`LANGSMITH_PROJECT` to your tracing project name instead of setting the two agent variables.If your account is in a region other than US (the default), also set`LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT` to the API URL for your region. Without this, your API key won’t be recognized and requests will fail to authenticate.Region URL GCP US `https://api.smith.langchain.com`GCP EU `https://eu.api.smith.langchain.com`GCP APAC `https://apac.api.smith.langchain.com`AWS US `https://aws.api.smith.langchain.com`For example, EU accounts: `export LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT="https://eu.api.smith.langchain.com"`.
For other providers, use the [`@traceable` decorator](/langsmith/annotate-code#use-%40traceable-%2F-traceable) to trace calls manually.

## 2. Build the app

The following app uses two LangSmith tools to add tracing:
- **Provider wrapper**: wraps the [OpenAI](/langsmith/trace-openai), [Anthropic](/langsmith/trace-anthropic), or [Gemini](/langsmith/trace-with-google-gemini) client so every LLM call is automatically logged as a nested span. The Gemini wrapper is in [beta](/langsmith/release-stages).
- **Traceable wrapper**: wraps a function so its inputs, outputs, and any nested spans appear as a single trace in LangSmith. Use `@traceable` in Python, `traceable` in TypeScript and Kotlin, and `Tracing.traceFunction` in Java.

The

`assistant` function calls a tool (`get_context`) to retrieve relevant context, then passes that context to the model. Using the traceable wrapper on both functions captures the full pipeline in one trace, with the tool call and LLM call as nested spans.
Create a file called `app.py`, `index.ts`, `App.java`, or `App.kt` with the following code:
- OpenAI

- Gemini

## 4. View your trace

In the
[LangSmith UI](https://smith.langchain.com?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=langsmith-signup&utm_content=langsmith-observability-quickstart), select your agent, go to

**Tracing**, and select the environment configured during setup. In a project-based workspace, open the project named by

`LANGSMITH_PROJECT`. For more information, see [Navigate agents](/langsmith/navigate-agents). Click the

`assistant` row to open the trace. The **Trajectory**tab shows the conversation as it was sent to the model. Select the

**Details**tab to see the full run tree, including the

`assistant` function with the `get_context` tool call and the model call nested inside it.
The outer span captures your `assistant` function’s inputs and outputs. The nested **get\_context**span (

**getContext**in TypeScript) records the tool call, and the model span (

**ChatOpenAI**,

**ChatAnthropic**, or

**ChatGoogleGenerativeAI**) records the exact prompt sent to the model and the response returned.

## Setting up LangSmith tracing for a LangGraph project

**Prerequisites**
1. LangSmith account + API key (smith.langchain.com → Create an API key)
2. A model provider key (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini)

**Step 1 — env vars** (`.env` or exported in shell):
```bash
# Legacy / project-based workspaces (still common, incl. self-hosted):
export LANGSMITH_TRACING="true"
export LANGSMITH_API_KEY="ls-..."
export LANGSMITH_PROJECT="my-graph-project"

# Non-US regions also need the endpoint, e.g.:
export LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT="https://eu.api.smith.langchain.com"   # AWS: https://aws.api.smith.langchain.com

# NEW: agent-based workspaces (cloud) — register an agent once, then address it;
# REMOVE LANGSMITH_PROJECT when using agent addressing:
export LANGSMITH_AGENT_ID="..."
export LANGSMITH_ENVIRONMENT="local"   # local | development | staging | production
```

**Step 2 — wire tracing into the graph.** Two tools:
- **Provider wrapper** — wraps the OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini client so every LLM call is a nested span automatically.
- **`@traceable` decorator** — wraps your node functions so inputs/outputs + nested spans appear as one trace.

```python
from langsmith import traceable

@traceable
def get_context(query: str) -> str:
    ...

@traceable
def assistant(state):
    ctx = get_context(state["query"])
    # call the wrapped LLM client here
```

With LangGraph specifically, wrapping the graph's nodes with `@traceable` (or using a traced LangChain LLM object) captures the whole execution path — inputs/outputs, branching through the graph, tool calls, errors, latency — as one trace with nested spans per node/step.

**Step 3 — run & view.** Execute your graph, then in the LangSmith UI: select your agent → **Tracing** → pick the environment → click a run. The **Trajectory** tab shows the conversation as sent to the model; the **Details** tab shows the full run tree (outer function → tool span → model span).

**Gotchas worth knowing**
- Do **not** mix legacy `LANGSMITH_PROJECT` and the new agent-addressing vars — pick one per workspace type.
- Wrong-region keys silently fail auth → set `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT`.
- Tracing is provider-agnostic; it works with any LLM, not just LangChain ones (via `@traceable`).

Sources: docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-quickstart (read directly), plus community corroboration (machinelearningplus guide, LangChain forum). Combined with the earlier LangGraph setup, you'd go: `pip install -U langgraph` → graph project → `langgraph.json` if using the platform → add the env vars + `@traceable` above.
